articles.title: Despite blue wave, not all Dems will commit to Schumer for majority leader just yet
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer speaks during a press conference on November 3, 2026, in Washington, DC. - Tom Brenner/Getty Images Chuck Schumer is confident he’ll continue leading Senate Democrats after they captured the chamber’s majority in dramatic fashion on Tuesday . Not all Democrats are so sure. During a post-election gathering Saturday in Washington, DC, two Senate Democrats — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan — declined to back Schumer for the job, and Slotkin said she would not rule out running herself. A third Senate Democrat who appeared at the conference, Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona, said he planned to support Schumer but echoed calls for Senate Democrats “to do things differently than we’ve done before.” “There should be no coronation of the next Democratic leader,” Van Hollen said. “I’ve said very clearly that we need to have a discussion in the Democratic caucus, we need to understand what the Democrats are going to do with this new responsibility and these new powers, and nobody should get a blank check without a full understanding of the caucus as to where we’re going to go.” Van Hollen said he has urged Democratic colleagues to “withhold commitments” until Schumer outlines his vision. And Slotkin said Democrats should not give Schumer quorum — the minimum attendance required to conduct Senate business — until he answers their concerns. Schumer remains a heavy favorite to become majority leader. He has no declared opposition and needs to win only majority support from Senate Democrats, whose ranks are poised to grow to at least 54 seats after Tuesday’s elections. But Saturday’s comments showed how even Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories could not paper over their long-simmering disagreements about who is best to lead them. That debate may be especially elevated among Senate Democrats looking at potentially running for president in 2028, a group that includes Van Hollen, Slotkin and Kelly. In addition to the reservations among the returning Senate Democrats, several incoming freshmen have vowed not to back Schumer for leader or at least withheld their support for now. Scott Colom , the Democrat in a Senate race in Mississippi that remains too close to call, has also been noncommittal on Schumer, calling for more geographic diversity among party leadership. In an interview with The New York Times that published Friday, Schumer said he did not expect to face any opposition. “Our caucus is focused on moving forward,” Schumer told the newspaper’s “The Daily” podcast. “Everyone’s very happy with what we all did.” Several Senate Democrats have already said Schumer has earned his right to return as their leader after the better-than-expected outcomes in Senate races. Kelly added his name to that list Saturday. “Chuck worked really hard to get this majority, so my plan is to support him,” Kelly told reporters after his appearance at the post-midterms summit, Crooked Con. Slotkin struck a different tone as she addressed the conference, which booed and jeered at the mention of Schumer’s name throughout the day. “If he wants to be majority leader, what is your plan for the first 100 days?” she said. “How are you going to do things differently so that Democrats get their sh*t together? If you can’t produce that, I’m not voting for you.” Asked whether she would run for the top job, Slotkin said it was “an open field, and I think those conversations are happening rapidly.” “I’m not ruling anything out,” she said. Van Hollen, for his part, suggested he was unlikely to run, even though at least one incoming freshman — Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan — has said he could support him. Van Hollen told CNN on Saturday that running for majority leader was “not my focus” and that he was instead weighing a 2028 presidential campaign. He said he has not heard “directly” from Schumer since the midterms but expected to speak to him in the coming week. Slotkin, who has long called for a “new generation of leadership,” said she hopes incoming freshmen follow the example she set in her first House run in 2018. She campaigned promising not to support Nancy Pelosi for House speaker — and followed through when she voted present in the speaker’s election in January 2019. “These people who just won in tough places, I think, will have a hard time, both as leaders but also just as politicians, going back on their word as their first thing that they do,” she said. articles.title: Eisenkot gets first chance to form Israeli government as Netanyahu fights to stay on
articles.summary: Nov 7 (Reuters) - Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, is fighting ‌to stay in office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an October 27 election but still emerged as the ‌largest bloc in parliament. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, whose support would give him a majority of seats in parliament. But Arab leaders, incensed ​by what they view as the racist policies of Netanyahu and his far-right allies, still nominated Eisenkot to try to form a government first — giving him the most endorsements. "President Herzog has invited Gadi Eisenkot to the President’s Residence, where he will be tasked with forming the government tomorrow," said the spokesperson of President Isaac Herzog, whose largely ceremonial role involves nominating a candidate to form a coalition after elections. In a post on X, Eisenkot wrote, "Now is the time ‌to form a national emergency government. I will do ⁠everything I can to ensure we are worthy." EISENKOT FACES LONG-SHOT BID TO FORM GOVERNMENT Weeks of protracted negotiations are expected to follow Eisenkot's nomination. He has 28 days to try to forge a government, with a possible 14-day extension. His potential ⁠pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab party votes on key issues; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu. Analysts say that all three options are unlikely to take shape. If Eisenkot fails, another ​candidate ​can try to form a government and if that candidate fails, parliament can nominate ​another. There is a deadline for the process of around ‌100 days. If no one succeeds, another election is held. Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Netanyahu's wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total, short of a 61-seat majority. Eisenkot's Yashar party emerged as the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, won just 48 seats. Two parties representing Israel's Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats. EISENKOT CRITICAL OF SETTLER VIOLENCE A son of Moroccan immigrants, Eisenkot, 66, would be the country's first prime minister from Israel's Mizrahi community, Jews who trace their roots ‌to the Middle East and North Africa. Reserved and media-shy, Eisenkot only entered politics in ​2022. He briefly served in Netanyahu's wartime cabinet following Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack on ​Israel before returning to the opposition. From opposition, he publicly rebuked Netanyahu ​over his leadership, including his management of the military campaign in Gaza, and has sworn that he would not ‌serve in government with him. Eisenkot's public standing is also bound ​up with the personal  price his family has ​paid since 2023: a son and two nephews were killed fighting in Gaza. Eisenkot highlighted his security credentials on the campaign trail, citing his "Dahiyeh doctrine" of responding to attacks with disproportionate force, which he deployed as a commander during Israel's 2006 war with Iran-backed Hezbollah in ​Lebanon. Eisenkot has criticised settler violence against Palestinians, which has ‌surged since 2023, raising tensions in Israel’s ties with Western states, and he opposes Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners Itamar Ben-Gvir and ​Bezalel Smotrich, who have both faced sanctions by some Western countries for inciting violence against Palestinians. (Reporting by Enas Alashray, Menna Alaa ​El Din and Alexander Cornwell; Editing by Cynthia Osterman and Timothy Heritage) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/israeli-president-picks-gadi-eisenkot-193153373.html

articles.summary: Two experienced skydivers were killed in a horrifying midair collision in Southern California after their parachutes became tangled just moments before landing, authorities said. The victims have been identified as Levi Pimentel, 29, of Illinois, and Georgia Jean, 56, of South Dakota, who died Friday afternoon after plunging to the ground near Lake Elsinore. The women collided about 150 feet above the ground as they approached the landing area, causing their parachutes to become entangled, according to Skydive Elsinore, the company involved in the fatal jump. Fire officials said both skydivers suffered major traumatic injuries and were found near the airfield already receiving medical attention. Josh Hall of Skydive Elsinore said the women were experienced, licensed skydivers and suffered no equipment failures. articles.title: Judge wants to know if Trump officials lied about plans for his D.C. golf course
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge said Saturday she intends to appoint an ex-top federal prosecutor in the nation's capital during President Donald Trump's first term to investigate whether she was purposefully misled by lawyers and administration officials in a lawsuit challenging one of his prized Washington construction projects, the renovation of a historic public golf course along the Potomac River. Jessie Liu, a former U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, would examine whether officials with the Interior Department and the National Park Service and attorneys with the Department of Justice violated ethics or misled U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes during the course of the case that was initiated in February by the DC Preservation League and two golfers. The Republican administration plans to close the East Potomac Golf Course and park on Nov. 15 with the intention of constructing a “World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events." An injunction issued by Reyes last month temporarily bars the government from removing or damaging any additional trees on the course and the administration must give 10 days’ notice in writing before making any “irreparable modification” to any “forms or features” of the course while the lawsuit is active. Reyes is giving each side a chance to be heard on her plan to name Liu as special master in the case. They must do so in writing by Friday, when the next court hearing in the dispute is scheduled. Reyes, who was nominated by Democratic President Joe Biden, wants to know whether federal officials lied about the extent of renovation plans during months of hearings. She also wants to know if they were truthful about various steps they took, including cutting hundreds of trees early last month. She announced during a hearing Oct. 30 that she was starting a formal investigation of the government's conduct. Earlier in the case, she had rejected numerous motions from the plaintiffs to step in, saying she trusted the government attorneys. As the city's chief federal prosecutor, Liu oversaw some of the matters referred to her office by then-special counsel Robert Mueller during his investigation into possible ties between Trump’s 2016 campaign and Russia. Trump later nominated her to be associate attorney general, the third-highest ranking Justice Department job. Liu withdrew from consideration after running into opposition on the Republican-led Senate Judiciary Committee because of her past membership in a lawyers’ group that has supported abortion rights. She eventually resigned from the group because, she said previously, it took left-leaning positions, and she is now part of her own law firm, Liu Shur Kravis LLP. David Super, a law professor at the Georgetown University Law Center, said the initiation of a formal investigation by a judge to look into the conduct of a trial's participants "can be a precursor to holding someone in contempt of court.” Super said it also is a reflection “of the difficulty she had in determining who initiated the tree-cutting in defiance of the assurances DOJ provided. She doesn’t have the time to keep holding long, complex hearings and so wants a special master to narrow the issues.” Reyes ordered the Oct. 30 hearing after multiple Truth Social posts by Trump indicated there were plans for the golf course and construction was expected to begin Nov. 15. Trump said the park would be closed for 15 months while work goes on. The presidential posts, which began Oct. 18, created a tense dynamic in multiple court hearings afterward when administration officials could not confirm the existence of the plans under questioning from Reyes. She eventually asked whom she should trust. The Justice Department filed notice Oct. 28 that the plans were real. ___ Bedayn reported from Austin, Texas. articles.title: Expanding on naval blockade, U.S. military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce
articles.summary: (Adds dropped word in paragraph 12) By Phil Stewart WASHINGTON, Nov 7 (Reuters) - Building on a months-long naval blockade on Iran, the US military said on Saturday it is launching a task force to help crack ‌down on Tehran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the ‌Caspian Sea. Task Force Iron Gate, which was first reported by Reuters, will be based in Tampa, Florida, and will coordinate with other US government agencies. ​Beyond movement of weapons, it will also focus on halting the flow of dual-use technologies used by Iran and stemming what Washington calls illegal revenue streams. The establishment of the task force is the latest illustration of how the US is still searching for ways to increase pressure on Tehran, more than eight months after launching with Israel a war against the Islamic Republic. While US ‌strikes have dealt devastating blows to Iran's conventional ⁠military and the US naval blockade has severely restricted its crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz and the Arabian Sea, Iran still poses a formidable threat to the region and its ⁠rulers have tightened their grip on the country. IRAN'S SECRET NETWORK A Reuters investigation found Iran has created a secret network of military agencies to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, evading both the US naval blockade and Western ​sanctions. The ​material entered Iran by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from ​Russia, by truck from Central Asia, and by freight ‌planes from China, the Reuters investigation showed. US Central Command said the task force will coordinate with other government agencies. A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that was expected to include the Treasury, State and Justice Departments but also the intelligence community. "Strengthening CENTCOM’s collaboration with US interagency partners will further constrain Iran’s ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," Admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of Central Command, said in a statement. Central Command estimated that its ‌naval blockade has prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in ​crude oil. Still, Iran has proven resilient and gloated following US midterm election ​results that punished Trump's Republican Party, giving control of ​Congress to opposition Democrats. Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for electoral rout, and ‌appeared to question whether the conflict was worth it. Mediators ​have intensified efforts in recent ​days to end the war between Iran and the United States amid fears it could reignite after the US midterm elections. Trump has been threatening to carry out a new offensive against Iran, putting countries in the Gulf ​on edge, since Tehran has threatened broad ‌retaliation against Gulf infrastructure. Reuters has reported that US intelligence assessments in recent months have indicated that renewed strikes ​on Iran would not fundamentally change Tehran's negotiating position or lead to the fall of Iran's government. (Reporting ​by Phil Stewart; Editing by Andrew Heavens and Tomasz Janowski) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/exclusive-expanding-naval-blockade-us-133922238.html

articles.title: Trump ally Laura Loomer reportedly charged up to $5,000 for political posts
articles.summary: The right-wing activist Laura Loomer has been paid by private clients to make political posts on social media without publicly disclosing the payments, according to a former campaign aide to President Donald Trump and three others familiar with the arrangements, shedding light on what they say is a business practice of one of the Trump administration's most influential online firebrands. The allegations were made by Alex Bruesewitz, an adviser to Trump's 2024 campaign, and three other people who spoke on the condition of anonymity. Two of the three people said they had paid Loomer directly to post political messages on her X account, where she has 1.9 million followers. The third said they had overseen clients who paid her to post on the account. The three spoke on the condition of anonymity. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. Bank transaction emails and a wire transfer statement reviewed by The Washington Post appear to show four payments totaling more than $60,000 sent to Loomer and a Florida-based company registered in her name, King Breaker Media, since May of last year. The documents do not specify the purpose of the payments, but two people familiar with the arrangements said they were for political posts. Loomer, one of Trump's best-known online acolytes, denied to The Post that she is paid to post on social media. She instead described herself as a journalist and activist and disputed the idea that she is an influencer paid to promote any political cause. The new claims about Loomer's influence business could add fuel to a growing debate about the little-regulated industry of political messaging on social media, where influencers on both sides of the aisle have operated in a legal gray area between advocacy and advertising. Bruesewitz first posted his allegations on X on Thursday. Many of the details about Loomer's alleged online influence operation have not been previously reported. Bruesewitz said in an interview with The Post that he had paid Loomer for tweets last year. He said the money had been sent through his political consulting firm, X Strategies, for posts related to policy issues. He declined to specify what clients. Despite brokering these deals himself, he believes that they should require clearer disclosures and have "gotten out of hand." Loomer disputed Bruesewitz's account and said that his firm contacted her last year offering to pay her for research. "He paid me to make a one-page research document for him, and then he wanted me to distribute the information. And that's what I did," Loomer said. Asked where she was expected to distribute the research, she said, "Either X or maybe an article." When asked how that was different from being paid to tweet, Loomer said she had actually been told to create the research document but that Bruesewitz had said he would have it distributed. Loomer accused Bruesewitz of "lashing out" at her because of her political beliefs. Bruesewitz and the three other people declined to publicly share the tweets they said Loomer had published to maintain the privacy of their clients. But The Post reviewed a selection of the tweets under the condition that they not be revealed publicly. Two of the people said that Loomer charges $3,000 to $5,000 per tweet, and sometimes more. Loomer said she does not have set pricing for consulting work. "I certainly don't charge $5,000 for a tweet," she said. The four people who had paid or oversaw payments to Loomer for posting political statements on social media said she is an effective, if sometimes unpredictable, messenger and a key way of trying to get a line directly to Trump. Jared Holt, a senior researcher at Open Measures, a platform that measures the spread of online extremism and disinformation, agreed. "This is somebody that has a tremendous amount of influence and access to the president's ear," said Holt, who studies the far right. Loomer said in an interview Thursday night that she could not discuss the terms of her work with most of her clients due to confidentiality agreements and the fact that her accountant handled her invoices. "I'm not some influencer that makes money from tweeting. My business is public affairs and opposition research," she said. "I also have a media company. It's not illegal to make a living in America." Roughly one hour after The Post discussed the claims with Loomer, she announced on X that she is taking a hiatus from her online show, "Loomer Unleashed," so she could pursue a more "healthy work life balance" and prepare for her upcoming wedding. "I just need to step back, recharge, refocus, and be present in my own life and my own mind with peace and clarity for a little while," she wrote. Loomer said the announcement had been scheduled in advance. Loomer, 33, has traveled with Trump and met privately with him in the Oval Office during his second term in office. Detractors within the administration have taken issue with Loomer's relationship to the president and have lamented that several high-ranking defense and national security officials have been dismissed after she has publicly rebuked them, often on her X account. Trump last year called Loomer a "very nice person" and a "patriot." After the White House fired aides on the National Security Council staff last year whom Loomer had accused of disloyalty, Trump denied that she was involved in the dismissal but acknowledged she had made some firing recommendations and said, "Sometimes I listen to those recommendations." The White House declined to comment. The Federal Trade Commission requires bloggers, influencers and other online figures to disclose when they have been paid to endorse a product, but the agency doesn't have jurisdiction over political ads. Some advocacy groups have called for stronger regulations around paid political content. The Campaign Legal Center last year petitioned the Federal Election Commission to consider requiring "paid for by" disclosures on influencers' political posts, saying they could help voters better assess the content they see online. California Gov. Gavin Newsom recently signed legislation that will penalize influencers who post paid political messages without disclosure. The general lack of transparency among political influencers, Holt said, "further degrades confidence in what people see online and how genuine it may be, or how representative it may actually be of the communities that these various influencers purport to speak for." Loomer has frequently said her bulldog advocacy reflects her genuine views, telling The Bulwark in May 2025 that she was "not paid for [her] posts." One person who said they had paid Loomer to tweet on behalf of clients said she was deliberate in her work and would only tweet if she agreed with the position. The person said not every client wanted to work with her because they believed she was polarizing but that some had hired her assuming she had an audience in the White House. The person added, however, that Loomer was like a "nuclear bomb." "You have to be careful how to use that," they said. "It's effective but also turns a lot of things to s--- if you're not careful." Loomer said she took that as a compliment. "I'm glad people find me to be effective and think I have a good reach," she said. "I'm not going to apologize for monetizing the fact that people fear me." articles.title: Wisconsin trooper released from ICE custody after 'dramatic experience'
articles.summary: A 21-year-old South African-born Wisconsin State Patrol trooper who was detained Nov. 5 by federal immigration agents was released from custody Nov. 6, according to his attorney. Attorney Marc Christopher confirmed to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel that Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe, who was traveling to visit family with a valid work permit, had been released from the Dodge County Jail and was awaiting a ride from his supervisor, the head trooper in Tomah. Christopher said Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision, which requires him to periodically check in with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. He will also likely be subject to electronic monitoring, potentially through an application on his cellphone rather than an ankle bracelet. Christopher said he plans to speak with Van Der Merwe to discuss the next steps in his case. He expects Van Der Merwe will eventually share his experience publicly but wants to give him time to readjust following his release. "I just told him I wanted him to get back, get reacclimated, just get settled, because I know he's gone through a very dramatic experience," Christopher said. Van Der Merwe came to the U.S. from South Africa with his family on visas at age 14, Christopher said. His family has been waiting seven years for their asylum case to be heard. Earlier, Christopher slammed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for detaining a Wisconsin law enforcement officer who has permission to work, saying he was "flabbergasted" by the agents' decision to use its resources to target Van Der Merwe. "I almost can't even believe that they would be so brazen as to do this. But they are," Christopher said. "There's no reason for them to detain him other than to indiscriminately pick up as many people as they can." Van Der Merwe, who lived in New Mexico with his family, wanted to serve in the U.S. military, but could not because he was not a permanent resident, Christopher said. He graduated with a degree in criminal justice in New Mexico, then researched states where he could do similar work with his status and found Wisconsin. Van Der Merwe was living in Onalaska and working in Tomah for the Wisconsin State Patrol over the past year. His work authorization is valid until 2030. Attorney disputes ICE's assertion about legal status ICE's argument is that Van Der Merwe – as a teenager in the U.S. with his family – overstayed his visitor's visa. "He entered the country in March 2019 with legal permission to stay until September 2019. In defiance of our nation’s laws, he overstayed his admission," a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said in a statement. "Work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the U.S." Christopher pushed back on that assertion. "That is just absurd and ridiculous," Christopher said. "They've been here lawfully. They have been waiting for their application to be adjudicated and to be decided by immigration." The family, who are White South Africans, had applied for asylum on the grounds they were persecuted. A family member had been attacked, Christopher said. Van Der Merwe did not decide to come to the U.S. himself, as he was brought by his parents, and he chose a career in law enforcement to serve his new country, Christopher said. ICE agents detained him Nov. 5 at the Dane County Regional Airport just after he went through security, Christopher said. He was traveling to visit his family in New Mexico. Agents handcuffed him, shackled his legs and put him in a van and drove him to Dodge County Jail, which holds ICE detainees. Christopher said it seems that the Transportation Security Administration tipped off ICE when he bought his ticket, and agents met Van Der Merwe at the airport. Christopher has heard of ICE making arrests at the Milwaukee and Appleton airports through similar tip-offs, he said. Lawyer hopes Congress changes the way ICE can operate Under the Trump administration, ICE has not been setting bond for detainees voluntarily unless a judge orders it. Trump administration policy changes have made many detainees ineligible to even seek bond and leave detention. Christopher said he hopes Wisconsin's congressional delegation takes note of the case and institutes changes to the way ICE can operate. He was critical that ICE would use its resources to arrest Van Der Merwe, then hold him in custody. "You're going to use your resources to go after this guy? You're going to use our tax dollars to detain this guy? It doesn't make any sense," Christopher said. As part of its summer surge in street arrests in Milwaukee, ICE arrested a 20-year-old Milwaukee man, Giovanni Sosa, who had lived in the U.S. since age 4 . In detaining him, ICE gave him paperwork that said – at age 4 – he had overstayed his visa. Sosa spent a month in detention at the Dodge County Jail as he waited for the chance to post bond. articles.title: Trump officials weigh major overhaul of National Park and Fish and Wildlife services
articles.summary: The Trump administration is considering a major reorganization of the National Park Service and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, according to internal documents reviewed by The Washington Post. Staff are meeting this week and next to discuss a “realignment” of the two agencies, the documents show. One meeting regarding the National Park Service will discuss “pending duty station changes,” referring to the locations where staff report to work. But the documents do not specify whether certain offices would be closed or moved, or whether any employees would be fired. The Interior Department, which oversees the agencies, did not respond to a request for comment. Get Climate Coach newsletter News and guidance on climate, science and technology. Sign up for free Public land advocates fear that the changes could further hurt agencies that have already seen major staffing cuts since Trump began efforts to shrink the federal government by hundreds of thousands of employees last year. “I think from their perspective, it seems as though that they’re trying to find efficiencies by consolidating staff within DOI that maybe served different functions across these agencies,” said Ed Stierli, vice president of government affairs at the National Parks Conservation Association, an advocacy group. “But I think in reality, it just seems to be causing more confusion and chaos. ” While the administration has considered differing plans to overhaul the Park Service since last year, including one reported in September by the Washington Sun, plans to reorganize the Fish and Wildlife Service are more recent. Fish and Wildlife manages more than 500 National Wildlife Refuges across the country, spanning 93 million acres. A Fish and Wildlife Service report published on Friday recommends the agency “reduce headquarters and regional office staffing and reallocate positions to refuge operations, prioritizing the people needed to manage habitat, maintain facilities, support public access and protect resources.” An internal communication to Fish and Wildlife Service staff on Friday, reviewed by The Post, states that the recommendations in the report “give us a path forward” and that “our next responsibility is to turn them into practical actions.” In March, the administration initiated a reorganization of the U.S. Forest Service, which includes relocating its headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City and hundreds of employees with it. The plan would also close some research stations and regional offices as it transitions to state offices. A judge has put that plan on hold , as well as a wider reorganization of the Agriculture Department that oversees it, amid legal challenges. Ron Johnson accuses Trump administration of corruption Trump ally Loomer was paid thousands for political tweets, people familiar say Her Statue of Liberty tour was supposed to be upbeat. Then she erupted. At the Park Service, the administration has withheld millions in funding and cut Park Service staff by about a quarter, sometimes leading to long lines, fewer tours and dirty bathrooms at parks. “When you talk about changing duty stations for example, are they just trying to cripple this agency?” Stierli asked. “Why would you try and sow chaos into an agency that is already stretched well beyond capacity trying to fulfill its mission?” Bill Wade, executive director of the Association of National Park Rangers, which represents current and former Park Service employees, said that agency employees have had to live with the uncertainty and stress that major restructuring might be coming, possibly including layoffs, since the launch of the DOGE Service last year. Based on the limited information about the current reorganization being considered, “it’s too little to try to determine what the impact would be on the service or employees,” Wade said. It is unclear whether the current reorganization plans for the National Park Service had been significantly revised from earlier proposals. Layoff plans last year at the National Park Service, which have not been independently verified by The Post, were ultimately never carried out. Stierli said that the administration appeared to “pump the brakes” on the plans two months ago, but it may now be feeling a new sense of urgency to restructure the agency with Democrats about to take control of Congress. “Come January, you’re going have a new Congress who’s very eager to do oversight and pry into the National Park Service to look and see how staff are being organized, where is the budget for the Park Service going,” Stierli said. In spending bills, congressional Democrats could write in provisions demanding approval over any restructuring in agencies, or at least to be notified, he said. “We’re certainly hopeful that Congress uses this oversight power here, because I think what’s highly unusual is there’s been zero transparency,” Stierli added. “When there is zero transparency, it creates this confusion.” This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://www.washingtonpost.com/climate-environment/2026/11/07/trump-officials-consider-revamping-national-park-service-fish-wildlife-service/

articles.title: Poland shooting leaves 6 dead and 16 wounded as minister calls it an 'act of terror'
articles.summary: KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — A Polish man with far-right views drove into a busy central square in Krakow on Saturday and opened fire, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him, authorities said. The attack, which Poland’s defense minister described as an “act of terror,” happened in Main Square, which is in the heart of Krakow’s Old Town and is a major tourist hub in the country’s second-largest city. The 25-year-old attacker drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each stop with an automatic weapon, authorities said. Although they didn’t release his name, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the man holds “very radical” and “ultranationalistic” views. "Everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” Kierwiński said at a news conference. Hours after the attack, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said authorities found the bodies of three of the suspect's close family members — two women and a man — inside of his home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow. “We have the next acts of this tragedy,” Tusk told reporters. Four women and two men were killed in the Krakow attack. At least three of the women were Polish, and one of the dead was a U.K. citizen, authorities said. Police were still trying to identify the other two people who were killed. A total of 13 people were hospitalized in serious condition, authorities said, though that figure may include the gunman, who underwent surgery after the attack. It’s unclear how many of the injured were shot. Two of them were treated and released within hours of the mass shooting. Two police officers were seriously injured, Kierwiński said. Five non-Poles were also injured, police commander Marek Boroń said. People were wounded at several locations The attacker wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest, and used a military-type long gun, Krakow police spokesperson Katarzyna Cisło said. Police found other weapons and ammunition in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said. The attacker engaged in a “wild ride” around Main Square, which is why people were wounded at several locations, said Cisło, adding that the gunman appears to have acted alone. Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday. He vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy. “The square will belong to us again,” Gibała said in a video posted on X. Mass shootings are rare in Poland Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims. In one video, a police officer is seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who is lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse himself to the ground. Photos showed a Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter after it landed in the square. It wasn't immediately clear whether the gun used in the attack or those found in the attacker’s car are legal. Around 411,000 people hold gun permits in Poland, which has a population of 37 million, and interest in gun ownership has been rising. Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland. However, in mid-October three attacks at schools in the central province of Mazovia took place within four days , leaving one person dead and many wounded, including children. The Krakow attacker's military gear, guns and overall look were similar to those of other “extreme right lone actors” committing attacks around Europe, said Kacper Rekawek, a senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague. “We have had attempts before, but now we can say that these kinds of attacks have become successful in Poland.” Warsaw mayor Rafał Trzaskowski announced increased security measures, including road barriers, along main streets in the old town in the Polish capital in the aftermath of the Krakow attack. ——— Ciobanu reported from Warsaw, Poland, and Dazio reported from Berlin. articles.title: Peltola campaign sues Alaska for rejected ballot records as Senate race stays tight
articles.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign is suing the state of Alaska to obtain access to records for absentee ballots that were rejected by the Alaska Division of Elections, a new court filing shows. Peltola’s campaign said they previously requested records of the rejected ballots on multiple occasions but were denied access. “Plaintiff cannot ensure that its voters’ lawful votes were properly counted without knowing whose absentee ballots were rejected or questioned, and why,” the lawsuit reads. “Each hour and each day that Defendants deny Plaintiff the requested records to which it is entitled costs Plaintiff the opportunity to help ensure that qualified voters have their ballots counted.” Peltola currently leads Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) in the Alaska U.S. Senate race by just over 600 votes, but with approximately 30 percent of the vote still outstanding, according to The Hill's partner Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ). No winner has been projected in the race as of Saturday morning. The Division responded in a release on Friday, saying voters who have had their ballots rejected have not yet had access to the information, therefore, the campaign should not be able to have access yet either. “Alaska’s constitution and laws do not require the Division to provide this information in the manner requested by the campaign. Releasing preliminary information in the manner sought by the lawsuit would create additional burdens during ballot processing and could delay the timely counting of votes,” the release said. The Alaska Senate race has already been the subject of litigation after the Trump administration sued to block certification of the election if Sullivan loses, arguing that the presence of a candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. could confuse voters. A judge dismissed that lawsuit ahead of Election Day, but the administration vowed to appeal. The vote count in Alaska will continue for several more days , as ballots in Alaska can arrive up to 15 days after the election if they came from outside the country, so long as they are postmarked by Election Day. More votes in Alaska do not have to be reported until Nov. 10, but may be reported incrementally before then. Final votes must be reported by Nov. 18. If no candidate has greater than 50 percent of the vote by that point — no candidate currently does — the state will run an instant runoff using ranked choice voting. The tabulation eliminates the last-place candidate and redistributes their voters’ second, third and fourth-choice preferences. The process repeats until a candidate has a majority. If Peltola wins the Senate race, it would be the eighth flip for Democrats in the Senate after a strong performance on Tuesday night. Votes are also still being counted in the Mississippi Senate contest where Democrat Scott Colom leads the incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved. articles.title: 未来两年“战斗到底”还是“极限谈判”？白宫人事频繁更迭，“坡脚”特朗普摆出“强硬姿态”
articles.summary: 共和党在中期选举中遭遇历史性惨败后，特朗普非但没有向选民释放的不满信号妥协，反而在一周之内完成了一轮强硬色彩鲜明的人事洗牌——以强硬派干将Stephen Miller取代Susie Wiles出任白宫幕僚长，并公开邀请UFC总裁Dana White担任新闻秘书。这一系列动作，向外界传递出一个清晰信号：在剩余两年任期内，特朗普摆出“强硬姿态”。 Miller的晋升被多名前特朗普政府官员和共和党人士解读为一次对民主党的“宣战”。 前白宫幕僚长Mick Mulvaney直言，此举向外界发出了“明确信息”—— 白宫将在未来两年继续优先行使行政权力 。与此同时，民主党众议院少数党领袖Hakeem Jeffries和参议院少数党领袖Chuck Schumer均措辞激烈地予以回击， 后者表示民主党多数将“每一步都与他对抗”。 这场人事地震发生在中期选举结束后不到一周。 特朗普在选举夜公开批评Wiles，随后将其扫地出门，转而将被视为“MAGA永恒之火”的强硬派Stephen Miller推上核心位置。与此同时，白宫新闻秘书一职持续空缺，Dana White的潜在入局更令外界对特朗普政府的对抗风格浮想联翩。 据 新华社 报道，特朗普7日在社交媒体上发文，宣布已邀请Dana White担任白宫新闻秘书，称其将是一位“与众不同”的新闻秘书，并表示需要他和他的助手来“抵御疯狂的左翼势力”。 中期选举惨败后，特朗普选择“加倍押注” 据《纽约时报》报道，在共和党于本次中期选举中遭遇“半个世纪以来最决定性的政治溃败”后，特朗普在最初几天表现得相对低调，甚至释放出愿与民主党合作的信号，称双方或许可以在移民问题上达成协议。 然而，这种姿态仅维持了数日。 周五，特朗普宣布解除Susie Wiles的幕僚长职务，以Stephen Miller取而代之。 这一转变被《纽约时报》描述为特朗普 “转向熟悉的动作：更多MAGA” 。 特朗普在离开白宫前往佛罗里达时表示，“我想做出改变”，称Wiles做了“很好的工作”，但“有时候在生活中，你必须做出行动”。当被问及希望Miller与Wiles有何不同时，他仅表示“把事情管好”。 值得注意的是，特朗普本人并未公开承认选举失败与自身政策的关联。据报道，知情人士透露，他在选举夜的东厅观选派对上当众批评Wiles，并私下将选举失利归咎于政治顾问，而非自身的政策路线。 Miller晋升：行政权力的“加速器” Stephen Miller的晋升，在特朗普圈子内外均被视为一个具有深远意涵的信号。 作为特朗普第二任期内最具影响力的政策推手，Miller是强硬移民执法行动的主要设计者，也是将行政权力运用推向极限的核心力量——包括在加勒比海和东太平洋对被其与特朗普定性为"外国入侵"的小型船只实施轰炸。 据The Hills报道，Miller的盟友表示，他对与国会民主党妥协毫无兴趣，并已准备好应对来自国会山的传票和调查。他的首要任务，据悉是重建破碎的MAGA联盟，并推进能够激励2024年选民的政策。 前特朗普政府国内政策委员会主任、现Covington & Burling LLP高级顾问Joe Grogan表示： “他们不会在行政权力、行政命令和法规上放慢脚步。Stephen会在所有这些方面积极推进。” Mulvaney则指出，如果特朗普真的想与新的民主党多数建立桥梁，“他可能会选择不同的方向”。 然而，也有声音对此表示忧虑。一位前特朗普政府官员直言：“我们完了。这与选民恳求共和党走的方向完全相反。”另一位曾与Miller共事的前白宫官员则描述他“聪明且固执己见，但在白宫工作人员中没有多少亲密朋友”，并称“大多数同事视他为某种程度上傲慢的独行侠”。 “谈判筹码”还是“真实意图”？ 围绕Miller晋升的解读，特朗普圈子内部存在分歧。一种观点认为，这是特朗普在政治上走向极端的真实信号；另一种观点则将其解读为一种谈判策略。 据The Hills报道， Joe Grogan持后一种看法： “特朗普是一个谈判者，通过选择Miller，他在谈判，因为他在展示力量，而非软弱。” 但无论动机如何，其市场含义是清晰的。一位共和党说客警告，Miller的晋升只会恶化白宫与国会山之间的关系： “总统有两个方向，一是与民主党国会合作，尝试完成一些事情；另一个是与他们开战。Stephen更像是一个‘开战派’。” 民主党方面已明确表态将全面对抗。众议院少数党领袖、即将出任众议长的Hakeem Jeffries（民主党，纽约州）在社交平台X上发文称Miller是“危险的仇外者和鲁莽的极端分子”，并要求“立即解雇他”。 参议院少数党领袖Chuck Schumer（民主党，纽约州）则写道，特朗普“从历史性的惨败中毫无所悟”，并警告民主党多数将“在每一步都与其对抗”。 分析认为，无论如何，随着民主党明年接掌国会两院，Miller主导的白宫与立法机构之间的正面交锋，将成为特朗普第二任期后半段的核心政治主题。 前幕僚长Susie Wiles的落幕 Susie Wiles的离开，标志着特朗普身边一个关键缓冲角色的消失。据《纽约时报》报道，Wiles是西翼历史上首位女性幕僚长，她帮助特朗普赢得2024年大选，并与总统建立了其四位第一任期幕僚长均未曾拥有的信任关系。 她曾在边际上影响特朗普的移民政策决策，并推动了国务卿Marco Rubio和财政部长贝森特的任命——两人均被外界视为政府内部的稳定力量。 然而，据报道，知情人士透露，Wiles与特朗普之间的裂痕早已存在。特朗普曾当着其他幕僚的面斥责她，批评政府在追查“泄密者”和推进对政治对手的起诉方面进展迟缓，甚至当着多名顾问的面指控她本人就是泄密者之一。 特朗普还开始将Wiles排除在人事决策之外，包括在选择新闻秘书一事上绕过她。Wiles的支持者则认为，对她的批评是一种“甩锅”行为——将一场主要由特朗普本人主导的政治和政策策略的失败，归咎于幕僚。 Wiles本人在社交媒体上发文，称在白宫为特朗普工作是“一生的荣耀”，并表示“虽然我的角色可能在改变，但我对总统和使命的承诺永远不会改变”。据报道，她将转入特朗普的外部政治运作机构，担任一个尚未明确界定的职务。 Dana White入局：对抗风格的“人格化”延伸 如果说Miller的晋升是特朗普政策路线的宣示，那么邀请UFC总裁Dana White出任白宫新闻秘书，则更像是这种对抗风格的“人格化”延伸。 据《华尔街日报》报道，White表示将于周一与特朗普会面讨论此事，但在UFC新闻发布会上被问及时，他仅表示“我已经有很多工作了”，态度暧昧。 特朗普此前已就这一职位接触过White，一位接近UFC总裁的人士证实了这一点。 这一提名背后有其逻辑： 白宫新闻秘书一职自8月Karoline Leavitt宣布离职后持续空缺， articles.title: 从预测市场到下一代交易所：400亿美元Kalshi明年冲刺IPO？
articles.summary: 近期，预测市场平台Kalshi完成G轮10亿美元融资，估值升至400亿美元，较今年5月F轮融资估值的220亿美元上涨约82%。随着估值迅速攀升，Kalshi已开始讨论IPO，最早或于2027年启动，但目前尚无明确上市时间表。 Kalshi成立于2018年，2021年获得美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）批准后正式运营，是美国首家受CFTC监管的事件合约交易所。其核心产品是围绕现实事件发行二元合约，用户可以交易某一事件是否发生，合约价格在0至1美元之间波动，并随市场预期变化。平台主要通过交易手续费获得收入。 得益于2024年美国大选带来的全国性关注，以及后续引入体育赛事合约（如世界杯、NFL赛季组合合约等）后对零售受众的成功触达，Kalshi年化营业收入已跃升至40亿美元以上，平台毛利率保持在90%的极高水平。在市占率方面，Kalshi在美国本土合规预测市场中长期占据超过90%的绝对主导地位。 Kalshi也在迅速拓展业务边界。今年5月推出加密永续期货成为首家将该加密衍生品引入美国受监管合规市场的交易所。随后于9月成功上线黄金和白银永续期货，并进一步向CFTC申报标普500股指、工业金属铜以及外汇等永续合约产品。 同时开展机构业务，9月已与约500家机构合作，剔除做市商后，机构交易量占平台总交易量约25%。此外，Kalshi与BitGo推出HODL Margining网络，允许机构客户以BTC、ETH及合格稳定币作为抵押品获取贷款，用于衍生品交易。 Kalshi的真正想象空间，在于成为传统交易所之外的新型金融平台

articles.title: 英伟达大劫案！超7600万元AI芯片和硬件离奇失踪
articles.summary: 据美国媒体6日报道，美国加利福尼亚州奥克兰市警方，目前正在调查一起涉及科技企业英伟达的货物被盗案件。 被盗物品为AI芯片和计算机硬件，价值高达1140万美元（约合7610万元人民币）。 分析人士表示，这可能是一起针对高科技企业精心策划的盗窃案。案情显示，一辆装载英伟达货物的卡车于今年8月29日从加州奥克兰出发，原定运往得克萨斯州沃思堡，提货流程符合原定安排，但卡车最终失联，受害人9月13日向警方报案。 警方追踪发现，卡车曾在途中多次停靠，单次停留时长达数小时，最终在加州东南部圣贝纳迪诺县失去踪迹。截至目前，警方尚未抓获任何嫌疑人。专家还表示，这批芯片在美国境外的售价接近美国本土的两倍，不排除赃物已经被转运出境的可能。据悉，这并非英伟达公司首次遭遇货物被盗事件。专家表示，这类案件的规模和复杂程度表明，相关犯罪手段日趋专业化，高价值科技产品的运输安全风险正逐渐凸显。 本文来源：央视财经 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 特朗普正在为一场更具对抗性的政治战做准备。在白宫新闻秘书一职连续出现人事动荡之后，他将目光投向了一个出人意料的人选——UFC终极格斗冠军赛总裁达纳·怀特（Dana White）。 据 新华社 报道，美国总统特朗普7日在社交媒体上发文说，他已邀请美国终极格斗冠军赛总裁达纳·怀特担任白宫新闻秘书一职。特朗普说，达纳·怀特将会是一名“与众不同”的新闻秘书。美媒报道说，目前尚不清楚达纳·怀特是否接受了特朗普的邀请。 据媒体报道，特朗普周六在帖文中称其为“伟大的Dana White，一位勇猛的战士”。 特朗普在帖子中明确表示，他需要达纳·怀特及其团队“抵御疯狂的左翼势力” ，措辞直接点明了这一人事安排背后的政治逻辑。达纳·怀特本人随后表示，计划于周一与特朗普会面，就这一职位进行讨论，但在UFC新闻发布会上被问及此事时，他仅回应称“我已经有很多工作了”，态度暧昧，目前尚不清楚他是否会接受邀请。 新闻秘书一职接连生变，特朗普急需“能打的人” 白宫新闻秘书的职位空缺，是此次达纳·怀特被提名的直接背景。 今年8月，原新闻秘书Karoline Leavitt宣布离职，此后该职位一直悬而未决。10月9日，特朗普宣布任命保守派评论员Katie Zacharia接任，但这一安排几乎在上任之初便宣告失败。据媒体报道， Zacharia仅在职五天便宣告离任 ，原因是其首次新闻发布会表现遭到广泛批评，加之此前曾以"律师"身份自居，却被披露实际上并未通过律师资格考试。 《华尔街日报》此前曾报道，特朗普私下抱怨，他在电视上缺乏足够多的政治盟友为其发声。这一背景使得他此次转向Dana White的逻辑更加清晰——他需要的不仅是一名新闻官员，更是一位能够在媒体战场上主动出击的"战士"。 特朗普在社交媒体帖子中的措辞耐人寻味。 他将达纳·怀特称为“violent Fighter and Warrior”（勇猛的战士），并明确表示需要他带来UFC选手助阵，“尽管其中一些人并非来自我们国家”，以此“抵御疯狂的左翼势力”。 这一表述与特朗普同期的一系列动作共同构成了一个清晰的政治信号： 在民主党即将于明年掌控国会、并誓言就腐败指控展开调查的背景下，特朗普正在主动强化其执政团队的对抗性色彩。 与此同时，一位接近达纳·怀特的知情人士透露，特朗普此前已就这一职位向其抛出过橄榄枝，此次并非首次接触。这意味着双方之间的讨论已有一定铺垫，但 达纳·怀特最终是否接受，仍有待周一会面后揭晓 。 特朗普与UFC的深厚渊源 特朗普与达纳·怀特及UFC之间的关系，可以追溯至二十余年前。 早在2000年代初期，特朗普旗下位于大西洋城的特朗普泰姬陵赌场便曾承办UFC赛事。彼时UFC因格斗风格过于激烈，在许多场馆遭到拒绝，特朗普的场馆是为数不多愿意接纳这项赛事的地方。这段早期合作奠定了两人关系的基础。 此后，达纳·怀特多次在政治场合公开力挺特朗普。 他曾在2016年共和党全国代表大会上为特朗普站台发言，并在2024年共和党全国代表大会上亲自为其介绍出场。 特朗普本人也多次以候选人和总统身份出席UFC赛事，这一系列公开亮相被认为帮助他在年轻男性选民群体中积累了支持。 今年6月，特朗普在白宫南草坪举办了一场笼中格斗赛事，作为美国建国250周年庆典活动的一部分。这场活动恰逢特朗普80岁生日，达纳·怀特坐在总统身旁，现场汇聚了军人、政府官员及特朗普盟友，被外界视为一次高调的政治展示。据报道，达纳·怀特此前曾就这一活动创意与特朗普会面，特朗普本人也亲自参与了活动细节的安排。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 共和党中选大败，币圈“好事到头”了？
articles.summary: 加密货币行业在华盛顿享受了两年的政治红利，如今随着民主党横扫国会中期选举，这一局面戛然而止。 据彭博11月7日报道，民主党赢得国会控制权后，加密行业将面临更严苛的立法条件、更密集的国会调查，以及对特朗普家族加密利益的深度审查。行业此前押注共和党换来的政策红利，正面临被重新定价的风险。 这一转折来得并不突然。今年9月，参议院未能推进《清晰法案》（Clarity Act）——这项本可为交易所和数字资产企业确立监管框架的立法，因特朗普的加密利益纠葛、稳定币收益分配争议及投资者保护分歧而陷入僵局。如今选举结果落定，这场争论的底层逻辑已经改变。 两年政治红利，一夜风云变 过去两年，加密行业在华盛顿获得了大多数行业梦寐以求的政治环境：一位将数字资产列为国家优先议题的总统、为更广泛应用铺路的监管机构，以及一个对行业议程高度同情的共和党国会。 特朗普不仅亲自推出数字资产产品，还多次邀请加密高管进驻白宫，将行业诉求纳入其政治议程。然而，他个人的加密财务利益也让行业在争取更广泛政治支持时屡屡受阻。 纽约大学斯特恩商学院兼职教授、前银行家Austin Campbell直言：“加密领域许多重要人物将自己与特朗普家族深度绑定，这些代价现在很可能要一一兑现。” 民主党接管，监管天平将向哪里倾 民主党控制国会后，已明确提出要对《清晰法案》进行重大修改，核心诉求包括：更严格的伦理限制、更强的消费者保护，以及赋予美国证券交易委员会（SEC）更大的数字资产监管权限。 这一方向与加密行业在共和党主导下争取的监管框架存在明显分歧。但Hyperliquid Policy Center首席政策官Adam Minehardt认为，这并非完全没有转机：“行业至少在初期会进入防御姿态，等待适应新的领导层。” 与此同时，民主党在国会的权力格局也在重塑。加密行业的强硬批评者、加利福尼亚州众议员Maxine Waters将在众议院金融服务委员会获得更大影响力；马萨诸塞州民主党参议员Elizabeth Warren预计将出任参议院银行委员会主席。 Minehardt说，“你将看到一个真正有实权的监督议程……我们已经从不同议员办公室收到信号——他们会拉动各种线头，看看通向哪里。” 昔日盟友，今成调查对象 加密行业的政治豪赌，如今也面临反噬。 2024年，加密游说团体向俄亥俄州参议员竞选投入数百万美元，试图击败民主党人Sherrod Brown。然而选举结果显示，Brown成功击败共和党参议员Jon Husted，重返参议院。据研究机构Capstone分析，Brown有望出任参议院农业委员会要职——该委员会负责监管商品期货交易委员会（CFTC），而CFTC正是加密行业的关键监管机构之一。 民主党控制国会还意味着对特朗普商业利益的调查权大幅增强。国会议员此前已就总统及其家族相关项目寻求信息披露。特朗普方面一贯否认其商业利益与总统职责存在冲突。 Healthy Markets Association首席执行官Tyler Gellasch指出，国会对监管机构拥有多种施压工具，包括预算权——可限制机构在特定政策议题上的资源投入。他表示，共和党此前曾用这一手段多年阻止SEC推行政治支出披露规则，民主党同样可以如法炮制。 既有成果难以逆转，但市场挑战犹存 尽管政治风向逆转，加密行业此前积累的部分成果并不容易被推翻。联邦稳定币法律的废除需要新立法，SEC和CFTC正在推进的数字资产规则制定工作也可在特朗普任期内继续推进，尽管未来政府可能重新审视相关机构决定。 市场层面的挑战同样不容忽视。比特币价格目前仍远低于历史高点，尽管特朗普执政期间的监管松绑和政治支持曾激发市场对"数字资产黄金时代"的预期。 安全问题也再度敲响警钟。币安近期遭遇黑客攻击，损失达63亿美元，此后通过企业财库资金及两只保险基金的组合方式基本补足了被盗加密货币。 威廉与玛丽学院兼职经济学教授Peter Atwater表示："加密行业需要让黑客攻击从头条新闻中消失。重复曝光会产生影响。这是否会推动民主党将监管钟摆拨回，更加强调安全性和稳健性，值得关注。" 跨党派路线，或成行业新出路 从更长远的视角看，加密行业的前景并不完全取决于与特朗普的政治同盟。数字资产已延伸至投资基金、稳定币支付和金融基础设施等领域，涉及众多机构投资者，其利益诉求超越任何一届政府的任期。 行业倡导者已开始主动强调跨党派立场。加密创新委员会首席执行官Ji Kim表示："数字资产始终是两党共同的议题，我们随时准备与两党新老议员携手合作。" 对于一个寻求跨越政治光谱、拓展用户群体的行业而言，减少党派标签，或许是一条比继续押注单一政治力量更为稳健的路径。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 野村：“蓝色浪潮”冲击美国数据中心，中国AI反而受益
articles.summary: 美国民主党在中期选举中横扫国会两院，市场对美国数据中心建设前景的担忧随之升温。但野村证券认为，这场政治变局对中国AI经济的净影响，可能恰恰是正面的。 据追风交易台消息，该行经济学家Ting Lu和Jing Wang在11月6日发布的报告中指出， 民主党"蓝色浪潮"将通过加强监管、保护电价等手段拖慢美国数据中心扩张，进而触发全球AI芯片价格回落，并缓解中国企业在高端芯片获取上的压力。"我们预计中国AI经济整体将从美国的蓝色浪潮中显著受益。"报告写道。 市场反应已经说明问题。选举结果出炉后两个交易日内，纳斯达克综合指数在第二个交易日单日下跌5.5%，创18个月最大单日跌幅；费城半导体指数（SOX）两日累计下挫近15%。英伟达两日合计跌约12%，美光科技跌幅约24%，SK海力士和三星电子在韩国KOSPI市场分别下跌9.5%和7.5%，并触发自动熔断机制。 摩根士丹利则在同期报告中提示，民主党控制国会并不意味着中美关系实质性缓和，但政策可预期性的提升。在AI投资策略上，该行更看好中国“自主可控”方向，而非依赖全球AI资本开支的出口链标的。 美国数据中心建设：监管收紧，扩张受阻 此次选举结果的直接影响，是美国数据中心建设面临更严格的政策约束。 据野村报告，民主党在多个数据中心建设关键州赢得州长职位， 新任领导层在竞选中大力强调消费者电费负担、能源可负担性与企业问责。 这意味着，数据中心开发商将无法再将电网升级、输电扩容和新增发电的资本成本转嫁给居民用户，财务负担将直接落在开发商自身。 该行指出，更严格的市政监管、禁止早期选址阶段签署保密协议，以及强制清洁能源采购要求，都将取代此前的快速工业开发模式。"一个新建超大规模数据中心从选址到并网所需的时间，将大幅延长。"报告称。 目前，美国数据中心建设规模庞大。据Cleanview追踪数据，美国共有逾4500个数据中心分布在超过1500个园区，其中约1418个已投入运营，564个在建，另有2555个处于规划阶段。商业地产公司Cushman & Wakefield的数据显示，当前在建容量已达创纪录的37.7吉瓦，规划管线更高达285吉瓦。 芯片价格下行：中国数据中心的意外红利？ 对中国而言，美国数据中心建设放缓带来的最直接利好，是AI芯片获取难度降低、价格压力缓解。 该行指出， "当美国云巨头大举扩张数据中心时，它们囤积了全球GPU、HBM和先进逻辑芯片的产能，收紧了全球供应，并推高了受限硬件在黑市和二级渠道的溢价。" 一旦美国数据中心资本开支放缓，这一局面将得到缓解。 该行认为，中国AI企业、云服务商和科研机构，将能够更便捷、更低成本地通过中间贸易枢纽获取相关GPU、HBM模组和先进封装材料。 分析师指出，在美国数据中心建设高峰期，亚洲物流枢纽的先进GPU和HBM模组灰市溢价往往高达标价的200%至300%。随着西方需求降温，"这些投机性溢价可能大幅崩塌，使中国买家能够以更合理的价格获取计算硬件"。 在基础设施层面，中国正推进由国家主导的全国AI数据中心网络建设，第十五个五年规划计划投入约2万亿元人民币（约2950亿美元），目标是到2028年将分散的区域算力设施整合为统一互联的网络，主要由中国移动、中国电信等国有电信巨头运营。与美国电网建设面临的地方阻力不同，中国依托"东数西算"工程，由国家电网统一协调，贵州、内蒙古、甘肃、宁夏等西部算力枢纽可直接获得低成本可再生能源供电，无需应对居民电价纠纷或电网并网排队。 摩根士丹利：看好 中国本土化和“自给自足”主题 摩根士丹利在同期报告中，对上述逻辑提供了补充视角，但基调更为审慎。 策略师Laura Wang和Vicky Wu指出，民主党控制国会不应被解读为中美关系的实质性缓和。"我们认为战略竞争和地缘政治不确定性将持续存在。" 策略师认为，此次选举的潜在正面影响，在于政策约束带来的可预期性提升。国会制衡将使大规模单边政策转向更加困难，降低关税反复升级成为主要双边政策工具的概率。 该行提出，应区分两类中国AI交易： 全球AI供应链的贝塔敞口（如光收发器等，主要跟随全球AI资本支出和美国政策审查），以及中国本土化和自给自足主题。 “我们更倾向于自给自足交易——它在中国国家政策优先级的框架下，同时享有供给和需求支持。” 摩根士丹利认为，持续的两党对华技术竞争，只会强化中国国内对技术自立的政策承诺，涵盖半导体、算力、电力设备和国内AI基础设施。 此外，摩根士丹利指出，与2026年上半年市场过度集中于AI交易相比，当前中国股市的投资机会更为均衡，涵盖消费及工业出口商、油价敏感的下游行业、医疗健康/生物科技，以及绿色能源板块。报告同时提示，中国股市目前估值处于历史绝对低位附近约10%的区间，各路资金近期已明显加大A股买入力度。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 复合氧化锆： 即将迎来自己的“六氟化钨”时刻？全球高端粉体市场市场迎来6000吨硬缺口
articles.summary: 全球最大的高端氧化锆粉体供应商日本东曹因原料耗尽宣布暂停供货，全球高端粉体市场被撕开约 6000吨/年的刚性缺口。这一事件的形态与六氟化钨此前面临的产业状况高度相似：同样是管制上游原料、卡住海外高端产能、价格与国产份额同步提升。 但六氟化钨靠的是价格弹性（涨价最高约14倍）与不可替代的工艺地位；复合氧化锆的真正护城河不是价格，而是长达2年的客户认证周期，海外瓷块厂每换一次粉体，需要重做烧结曲线、批次稳定性测试，并在欧盟 CE 与美国 FDA 重新走一遍合规流程。这意味着订单转移是单向上锁的，一旦完成切换就回不去。
